# requires: logging
#
# One property lets several processes on several machines append to one file:
# a whole record goes out in one write, so writers interleave whole lines rather
# than halves of two. A record too big for that cap has three possible fates and
# only one of them keeps the property and the evidence.
#
# `over` counts lines longer than the cap and `marked` counts lines carrying the
# shrink mark. The exact length of a shrunk line is not asserted, and must not
# be: two implementations shrinking by different amounts both keep the rule, and
# pinning the number would make one of them wrong for no reason.
machine file
auto A
cap A 512
record R 0
msg R 8000
write A R
held A
record S 0
write A S
held A

# expect 6: ok where=file [LOG-S6]
# expect 7: ok lines=1 over=0 marked=1 [LOG-S6]
# expect 9: ok where=file
# expect 10: ok lines=2 over=0 marked=1 [LOG-S6]
